ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the trapezoid $ABCD$ shown in the figure, $\angle ABC = \angle BCD$, $AD \parallel BC$, and $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$. If $AD = 3$ and $BC = 7$, what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw AE$\perp$BC at point D, and draw DF$\perp$BC at point F, then the quadrilateral AEFD is a rectangle.\\
In trapezoid ABCD, $\angle ABC=\angle BCD$, AD$\parallel$BC,\\
$\therefore$AB=CD, $\angle ADB=\angle DBC$,\\
$\because$BD bisects $\angle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle ABD=\angle DBC=\angle ADB$,\\
$\therefore$AB=AD=3,\\
$\because$AD$\parallel$CB, AE$\perp$CB, DF$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$AD=DF,\\
$\therefore$right $\triangle AEB\cong$ right $\triangle DFC$ (by HL),\\
$\therefore$BE=CF,\\
$\because$quadrilateral AEFD is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$AD=EF=3,\\
$\therefore$BE=CF= $\frac{1}{2}$(7−3)=2,\\
$\therefore$AE=DF= $\sqrt{AB^{2}-BE^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$BD= $\sqrt{DF^{2}+BF^{2}}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^{2}+5^{2}}=\boxed{\sqrt{30}}$,

Then reason: by the coordinate method, take B=(0,0), C=(7,0). Because AD∥BC and ∠ABC=∠BCD, the trapezoid is an isosceles trapezoid, so the upper base AD=3 is placed centered above the lower base BC. method.method_draft: Use an analytic-coordinate setup. From the image, take BC as the horizontal bottom base with B on the left, C on the right, AD as the shorter horizontal top base, and D the upper-right endpoint joined to B. From the text, use BC = 7, AD = 3, AD parallel BC, angle ABC = angle BCD, and BD bisects angle ABC. Place B = (0,0), C = (7,0). Since the equal base angles make the trapezoid isosceles, the shorter top base is centered over the bottom base, so A = (2,h) and D = (5,h). The angle bisector from B has direction equal to the sum of unit direction vectors along BA and BC: unit(BA) = (2,h)/sqrt(4+h^2), unit(BC) = (1,0). Since BD points in direction (5,h), set (5,h) parallel to (1 + 2/L, h/L), where L = sqrt(4+h^2). Comparing the vertical components gives the scale as L, so the horizontal component gives 5 = L + 2, hence L = 3. Then h^2 = 3^2 - 2^2 = 5, and BD = sqrt(5^2 + h^2) = sqrt(25 + 5) = sqrt(30).

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic cyclic-trapezoid/Ptolemy route. From the image, identify ABCD as a trapezoid ordered B-A-D-C around the boundary, with diagonal BD drawn from B to D. From the text, AD parallel BC and BD bisects angle ABC. Because AD is parallel to BC, angle ADB equals angle DBC. Since BD bisects angle ABC, angle ABD equals angle DBC. Therefore angle ABD = angle ADB, so triangle ABD is isosceles and AB = AD = 3. Also angle ABC = angle BCD makes the trapezoid isosceles, so CD = AB = 3 and its diagonals are equal, AC = BD; equivalently, it is cyclic. Apply Ptolemy to cyclic quadrilateral ABCD: AC · BD = AB · CD + AD · BC = 3·3 + 3·7 = 30. Since AC = BD, BD^2 = 30, so BD = sqrt(30).

raw_record.original_question: In the trapezoid $ABCD$ shown in the figure, $\angle ABC = \angle BCD$, $AD \parallel BC$, and $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$. If $AD = 3$ and $BC = 7$, what is the length of $BD$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw AE$\perp$BC at point D, and draw DF$\perp$BC at point F, then the quadrilateral AEFD is a rectangle.\\
In trapezoid ABCD, $\angle ABC=\angle BCD$, AD$\parallel$BC,\\
$\therefore$AB=CD, $\angle ADB=\angle DBC$,\\
$\because$BD bisects $\angle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$$\angle ABD=\angle DBC=\angle ADB$,\\
$\therefore$AB=AD=3,\\
$\because$AD$\parallel$CB, AE$\perp$CB, DF$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$AD=DF,\\
$\therefore$right $\triangle AEB\cong$ right $\triangle DFC$ (by HL),\\
$\therefore$BE=CF,\\
$\because$quadrilateral AEFD is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$AD=EF=3,\\
$\therefore$BE=CF= $\frac{1}{2}$(7−3)=2,\\
$\therefore$AE=DF= $\sqrt{AB^{2}-BE^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$BD= $\sqrt{DF^{2}+BF^{2}}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^{2}+5^{2}}=\sqrt{30}$,
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the lower base BC of trapezoid ABCD is horizontal, with B on the left and C on the right; the upper base AD is shorter and horizontal, with A at the upper left and D at the upper right; AB and CD are the two slanted sides; segment BD connects from the lower-left vertex B to the upper-right vertex D. Then reason: by the coordinate method, take B=(0,0), C=(7,0). Because AD∥BC and ∠ABC=∠BCD, the trapezoid is an isosceles trapezoid, so the upper base AD=3 is placed centered above the lower base BC. The difference of the base lengths is 7-3=4, with 2 on each side, so we can set A=(2,h), D=(5,h). Let L=|BA|=sqrt(2^2+h^2)=sqrt(4+h^2). Starting from B, the unit direction vector of BA is (2,h)/L, and the unit direction vector of BC is (1,0). Because BD bisects ∠ABC, the direction of BD is parallel to the sum of these two unit vectors, that is, the BD direction (5,h) is parallel to (1+2/L,h/L). Let the scale factor be k, then (5,h)=k(1+2/L,h/L). From the y-coordinate h=k·h/L, get k=L; substitute into the x-coordinate, 5=L+2, so L=3. Thus h^2=3^2-2^2=5. Finally BD=sqrt(5^2+h^2)=sqrt(25+5)=sqrt(30).
